help.description: TOW watches topics on torrent sites and hands new versions to your torrent client.
help.epilog:
exit codes (every command):
  0    done
  1    a wrong command or option
  2    done in part: a topic, a mirror or a step failed
  3    cannot run: config, passwords and tokens, the lock or a file is missing or broken
  130  interrupted (Ctrl+C)

“setup” is a command of the launcher ({launcher} setup): it rebuilds the environment after a
move or an update, with TOW stopped.
Every command explains itself: tow COMMAND --help

Nothing outside the TOW folder changes.

intro.text: TOW watches topics on torrent sites. When a topic page gets a new version, TOW hands it to your torrent client (qBittorrent, Transmission or Deluge) and tells the connected messengers. TOW itself downloads nothing and does not move files — the client does that.

s1.title: 1. Sections
s1.home: Home — the topics TOW watches: link, name, folder in the torrent client.
s1.sites: Sites — where the topics come from (rutor, kinozal…). A site can have several mirror addresses: if one does not answer, TOW takes the next.
s1.settings: Settings — torrent clients, notifications, how often to check, access from other devices, the service and backups.
s1.log: Log (the list icon in the header) — recent events. Passwords never get there. The log does not grow forever: {n} files of {size} each are kept.

s2.title: 2. How to add a topic
s2.step2: You can keep the suggested name and folder. The folder is where the torrent client saves the files.
s2.step3: TOW checks the topic at once and, if the client is reachable, hands it to the client; you get the message “… — added to the torrent client”.
s2.dot: The dot in a row is the result of the last check: green — all fine, blue — something new found, yellow — the site is temporarily unavailable (TOW will try again), red — your help is needed (the reason is under the name; open the row — click or tap it, or press Enter — for the full text), grey — not checked yet.
s2.icon: The site icon shows the site alone: a torrent client or folder error does not color it.
s2.step1: Home → + → paste the link to the topic page on the site.

s3.title: 3. How to add a site
s3.step2: The easiest way is to paste a link to any topic on that site — the fields fill in by themselves.
s3.step3: If the file cannot be downloaded without signing in, enter the site's login and password. They are stored encrypted.
s3.step4: The address you click in the site's row becomes the main one; the globe icon opens it.
s3.note: If a site address does not answer three times in a row, TOW skips it for an hour and tries the others; the “Check” button in the site's row ends this pause. When a site says “download limit for today”, TOW leaves it alone until tomorrow.

s4.title: 4. Notifications
s4.text: Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp and ntfy are in Settings → Notifications. Each has “How to connect” steps and a “Check” button. Every message goes to all connected messengers. If a messenger is unavailable, the message waits and goes out later by itself. The bell in the header: green — messages get through, red — some messenger did not accept a message, grey — nothing is connected.

s5.title: 5. Checks and the clock in the header
s5.text: Topics without a personal timer are checked automatically every {interval} (Settings → Checks). The header clock shows the next global check; a topic's own timer replaces that interval for that topic. The running TOW service restarts the web server if it fails. Every 10 minutes the watchdog checks the schedule and reports downtime and its cause; it does not restart TOW.

s6.title: 6. Backups
s6.night: Nightly backups are made automatically every night; if a backup fails, you get a message. You can choose the folder, including another drive or a network folder.
s6.create: Create a backup — a backup “just in case” before important changes. Restore first checks the backup and saves the current state.
s6.note: A backup holds the settings, topics, history and encrypted passwords. Downloaded files and the torrent client itself are not in it. The address, port and access from other devices stay as they are when you restore.
s6.file: TOW file (.towx) — a full encrypted copy of this TOW. Restoring it needs the same encryption key (keys/master.key): on another computer, put that key there first — it is not in the file, so keep it separately, for example on a USB stick. To move TOW to an install with a different key, use tow export and tow import in a terminal: their file is protected by a passphrase instead.

s7.title: 7. Access from a phone or laptop
s7.text: On this computer TOW opens without a password. From other devices — only with a password (Settings → Network access); a device stays signed in for 90 days. Access and the password can only be changed on this computer.

s8.title: 8. Where the data is
s8.config: — settings and the list of sites (without passwords).
s8.secrets: — encrypted passwords and tokens. The encryption key is kept apart from the data.
s8.note: An empty password field in a form means “keep as is”; saved passwords are never shown.

store.state_newer: state.json was written by a newer TOW (data version {found}; this TOW knows {known}). Update TOW or restore a backup made by this version; nothing was changed.
store.state_bad_version: state.json has a data version this TOW cannot read ({found}); nothing was changed. Restore it from a restore point or a backup.
store.no_master_key: The master key is missing, so the saved passwords and tokens cannot be opened. Put the key file back as keys/master.key in the install (or point TOW_MASTER_KEY_FILE at it), or bring it in with: tow keys adopt --from FILE. On a new install without saved passwords and tokens, run: tow keys ensure
store.key_path_outside_data: A relative TOW_MASTER_KEY_FILE path must stay inside the TOW data folder. Use an absolute path for an external key file.
store.key_unreadable: The master key file cannot be read. Check that keys/master.key (or the file TOW_MASTER_KEY_FILE names) is there and that this account may open it.
store.key_empty: The master key file is empty, so the saved passwords and tokens cannot be opened. Put the key back from your copy: tow keys adopt --from FILE
store.key_invalid: The master key is damaged or not a TOW key file. Put back the key the passwords and tokens were saved with: tow keys adopt --from FILE
store.no_cryptography: The cryptography package is missing from TOW's environment, so the saved passwords and tokens cannot be opened. Rebuild the environment: tow setup
store.secrets_write_failed: The passwords and tokens could not be saved. Check the free space and the access to the data folder, then try again.
store.secrets_damaged: The file of saved passwords and tokens is damaged and cannot be read. Restore it from a restore point or a backup.
store.secrets_unsupported: The file of saved passwords and tokens is in a format this TOW does not know (written by a newer version or another program). Update TOW or restore the file from a backup made by this version.
store.secrets_wrong_key: The master key in use does not open the saved passwords and tokens. Put back the key they were saved with: tow keys adopt --from FILE
store.legacy_unreadable: The old unencrypted {file} cannot be read. Correct or restore it, then run: {command}
store.legacy_left: The data folder holds both the encrypted {encrypted} and the old unencrypted {file}, and TOW uses neither while both are there. Delete {file}: the passwords and tokens are kept in {encrypted}.
store.migrate_needed: The passwords and tokens are still in the old unencrypted {file}. Encrypt them: {command}
store.readback_mismatch: The passwords and tokens were written, but did not read back the same. Try again; if it happens again, check the disk and the data folder.
store.legacy_remains: The passwords and tokens were encrypted into {encrypted}, but the old unencrypted {file} could not be deleted. Delete it by hand.
